authority_behaviour: tls13_enc appends the inner content type and AEAD-seals plain||type under type||version||length AAD.
tls13_dec strips the trailing zero padding, reads the last non-zero byte as the inner type, and returns content_len.
tls_psk_do_binder derives early/binder/finished keys and HMACs Hash(ClientHello up to the binders vector); the received binder must be hashsize bytes (extensions_srvr.c:1441-1448).
tls13_generate_secret is Derive-Secret(prev, "derived", Hash("")) then HKDF-Extract; labels, orders and lengths are unchanged.

boundary.reconstructed: One slice-based key schedule over the live connection: every key-schedule input and output is a Rust slice whose extent is the actual buffer; every secret-bearing stack copy is a single CleansedBlock owner; the record output is an OutRegion whose only unsafe construction is the caller-region proof and whose writes are bounds-checked. The digest handle (`*const EvpMd`), the connection pointer and the C input/output regions remain the named unsafe boundary.

aead_bounds.encrypt: tag_len is the cipher mandat (16 for the three suites); inner_len = len+1 checked <= TLS13_HS_BUF_LEN+1; rec_len = inner_len+tag_len checked <= u16::MAX; out_len = 5+rec_len checked; header/body/tag written through OutRegion::write/slot after capacity checks. Success now requires the AEAD update to have produced exactly inner_len ciphertext bytes, so the published record has no uninitialised gap.
aead_bounds.decrypt: ct_len < tag_len -> -1; ct_body_len = ct_len-tag_len checked <= TLS13_HS_BUF_LEN+1; tag = ct[ct_body_len..] is exactly tag_len; the plaintext block is plain_cap = max(ct_body_len,1); success requires outl == ct_body_len; the padding walk reads only the authenticated prefix.
aead_bounds.inner_type_and_padding: strip_record_padding returns Option<(content_len,u8)>; None for an all-zero plaintext (no type); on Some, content_len < plain.len() and plain[content_len] is the in-range type byte. content_len > out_cap is refused before the copy.
aead_bounds.s39_s40_verification: The S39 decrypt sink contract still holds: out is written only for content_len <= out_cap, never read, and only on authenticated success. This batch additionally removed the pre-existing typed slice over the uninitialised decrypt scratch and the typed slice over the caller's whole encrypt output (see defects).

boundary.transcript_ownership: hs_buf/hs_buf_len/hs_md_ctx remain single-owned by Ssl and released by SSL_free; transcript_update and tls13_init_transcript use checked prefixes and do not create a second live mutable alias. Stack transcript hashes are CleansedBlock<past> locals (one owner, wiped on every return).
boundary.key_material: early_secret/handshake_secret/master_secret/traffic secrets/resumption secret stay in their single Ssl fields; the traffic key and IV are derived into CleansedBlock<32>/<16> locals and copied into enc_key/enc_iv or dec_key/dec_iv through checked field prefixes. No secret is duplicated into a second long-lived owner.

unsafe_ops.before_after: tls13_enc.rs production `unsafe {` blocks 76 -> 77; #[cfg(test)] blocks 8 -> 13; total 84 -> 90. Production `unsafe fn` 36 -> 35 (select_secret removed). from_raw_parts 20 -> 9; copy_nonoverlapping 8 -> 3; raw .add()/as_mut_ptr() occurrences 39 -> 22.
eliminated: hkdf_extract / hkdf_expand_label / tls13_derive_key / tls13_derive_iv / tls13_derive_finishedkey raw pointer parameters: replaced by slices, so the extent is the buffer (11 from_raw_parts removed overall).
tls13_generate_secret(_md), tls13_generate_handshake_secret and tls13_generate_master_secret raw output pointers and from_raw_parts borrows of the connection's secret fields.

Traffic-secret derivation's raw ptr::copy_nonoverlapping of the transcript hash into handshake_traffic_hash/server_finished_hash and its from_raw_parts reads of the stored secrets (now checked field prefixes and copy_from_slice).

select_secret (a raw *const u8 return) and its unsafe block; tls13_change_cipher_state now selects a checked field prefix and installs key/IV with copy_from_slice instead of four ptr::copy_nonoverlapping calls.

tls13_psk_do_binder's raw msgstart/binderoffset deref, its raw `*binder.add(i)` compare read and its raw HMAC output: the transcript and both binder buffers are slices, and the received length is checked at the top of the function.
tls13_encrypt_record's `from_raw_parts_mut(out, out_len)` over the caller's whole record buffer and its slice indexing for the body/tag.

tls13_decrypt_record's `from_raw_parts_mut(plain, plain_cap)` over CRYPTO_malloc (uninitialised) memory; it now keeps a raw writable region until authentication and forms `&[u8]` only over the authenticated prefix.
write_handshake_message's three raw byte stores/copies; framing now goes through OutRegion::write.
relocated: OutRegion::new (one unsafe constructor: caller writable region, no overlap), OutRegion::write (bounds-checked copy) and OutRegion::slot (bounds-checked raw pointer for the AEAD output) - 3 narrow blocks, one caller-region contract.

The 9 remaining from_raw_parts sites: C input regions (transcript_update data, encrypt plain, decrypt ct, write_handshake_message body), C output region (transcript_hash out), the initialised inner-plaintext block, the authenticated decrypt prefix, and the two Finished secret inputs. Each has a SAFETY contract naming the boundary.
The remaining FFI calls (HMAC, EVP_*, EVP_MD_CTX_*, BIO-facing handshake write) are unchanged calls inside their documented blocks.
unsafe_ops.contract_coverage: Every production unsafe block carries a `SAFETY:` contract; undocumented_unsafe_blocks and unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn are unchanged, so cargo clippy --lib -D warnings is the mechanical evidence.

binder_verification.s29_finding: The pre-fix receiver read hashsize bytes through a bare pointer for a binder of any non-zero length (out-of-bounds read past the ClientHello).
binder_verification.remaining_paths: tls13_psk_do_binder is the only binder computation. It now takes `transcript: &[u8]` (hash input extent = the ClientHello prefix), `binder: &mut [u8]`, and `received: &[u8]`; it (1) requires binder.len() == EVP_MD_get_size(md), (2) for sign=false requires received.len() == hashsize, both before any secret is derived or any byte read, then (3) runs the full-length accumulation with slice indexing. The only production caller derives md_size from the resolved session ciphersuite (tls13_md_size(kind)), checks binder.len() == md_size and binderoffset <= hs.len(), and passes hs[..binderoffset] and calc[..md_size].
binder_verification.result: VERIFIED from this side; no out-of-bounds read remains on the binder path. The regression test fails deterministically pre-fix because the pre-fix code writes the computed binder into the output buffer before checking the received length (asserted untouched).

secret_cleansing.owner: CleansedBlock<N> is the single stack owner for HKDF scratch, early/binder/finished intermediates, traffic key/IV, transcript hashes, the Finished verify-data buffers and the keylog hex line; Drop is the only release and runs on every early return.
secret_cleansing.release_vs_cleansing: Heap plaintext blocks still use OwnedBuf::new_cleansed (CRYPTO_malloc + CRYPTO_clear_free), preserving the authority's release mechanism; the stack owner wipes before returning. A destructor that merely frees is not used for secret material.
secret_cleansing.failure_paths: Every refusal after a secret exists (failed HMAC, over-long label, missing transcript context, tag failure) drops the owners and wipes them; the test hook observed 4 cleansed blocks with 3 non-zero secret blocks on the tls13_finished_mac failure path.
secret_cleansing.constant_time: The tag compare and the binder compare remain full-length accumulations with no early exit; no secret-dependent branch was introduced. The padding walk branches on public padding bytes only, after authentication.

defects_found_and_fixed.finding: tls13_encrypt_record formed `&mut [u8]` over the caller's whole uninitialised record buffer (`from_raw_parts_mut(out, out_len)`) before writing it. The S39 boundary fixed the read path but this write sink still had the same class of UB.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: OutRegion keeps the region raw and raw writes are capacity-checked; no reference is formed over caller memory.

defects_found_and_fixed.finding: tls13_decrypt_record formed `&mut [u8]` over `CRYPTO_malloc` (uninitialised) scratch for the whole `plain_cap` before the AEAD wrote it; the S39 receipt described the block as a cleansed block, but new_cleansed is malloc, not zalloc.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: The plaintext stays a raw writable region until authentication; the slice covers only `outl == ct_body_len` authenticated bytes.

defects_found_and_fixed.finding: tls13_encrypt_record accepted a short AEAD update (`outl < inner_len`) and still published `out_len` bytes, which could include an uninitialised gap in the record.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: Success now requires outl == inner_len; the tag is placed only then.

compatibility_delta: Key-schedule outputs are unchanged: labels, derivation order, hash/HMAC inputs and lengths are identical. All changes are refusals on internal states that cannot arise from a valid record or binder: out-of-range digest lengths, a short/long binder, a short HKDF output, an AEAD update that does not fill the declared extent, and an all-zero inner plaintext. Record protection semantics, error values (-1), sequence advancement (only on success), and keylog formatting are unchanged.

discharged: Every AEAD extent is derived from a checked length against the actual buffer; the tag length is the cipher's mandated value.
An all-zero/truncated inner plaintext is refused; padding removal cannot produce an out-of-range type or length (structural Option + test).
A short, long or empty received binder is refused before any secret derivation or read (S29 regression control).
Secret-bearing stack copies have one cleansing owner on success and every failure path.
The encrypt path no longer forms a reference over the caller's uninitialised record buffer, and publishes only fully written bytes.
The decrypt path no longer forms a reference over uninitialised allocator memory; the padding walk sees only authenticated bytes.
The binder transcript extent is the slice length, not a separately asserted offset.
retained: `s: *mut Ssl` liveness/exclusive ownership is the caller's C ABI contract.
OutRegion::new's writable-and-non-overlapping caller region, and the raw input regions for encrypt/decrypt/transcript bodies, remain boundary preconditions.
transcript_hash's raw output pointer and the Finished functions' raw secret pointer remain C ABI inputs with stated extents.
The digest handle `md` must be a live EVP_MD; no safe caller can construct one otherwise.
The BIO/handshake write and EVP calls retain their own liveness contracts.
introduced: Refusal when an AEAD update does not produce the declared ciphertext/plaintext extent (impossible for the three reduced suites in practice).
Refusal when hs_md_len is 0 or greater than EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE before any secret slice is formed.
